facts.note: The maze across, outer wall to outer wall: 28 lanes-and-walls of 3 blocks (a lane 2 wide, a wall 1) plus the outer wall. Large enough that a loop's two sides stand farther apart than the warden hears (16 blocks), and that the walk to the gate fills the evening's middle.
The maze's play space inside its outer wall.
A lane 2 wide and a wall 1 thick: the warden walks a 1-wide lane as fast as a 2-wide one, so the width is for two players passing and for reading from the deck.
Three courses of stone under a hedge cap: a jumping player does not see over it, and it hides the 2.9-block warden from the lane but not its sound.
How far the warden hears a footstep, a landing projectile or a bell (warden-behaviour.md, sections 1 and 5). Every lure and every loop is sized against it.
The lookout deck and the bridge: 22 above the lanes, beyond the warden's sniff and its ranged attack (both 20 vertically), so the caller is never its target from the deck.
The bridge's deck from the east arm's end to the gate tower's parapet.

Each arm of the lookout's cross reaches this far out from the deck over the maze. Chosen by measurement: from the arms' rails a standing runner's head is seen in about 88 % of lane cells (70 % in the outermost band), against 38 % from the deck alone.
